name: Serum Protein Electrophoresis, Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency, and Wilson Disease

reference.source: Medical Biochemistry 5th ed / Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd ed
clinicalPearls: Serum albumin generates 80% of intravascular colloid oncotic pressure and acts as a transport carrier for bilirubin and drugs
Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (PiZZ genotype) causes protein misfolding in hepatocytes (cirrhosis) and panacinar emphysema
Hepatocyte PAS-positive, diastase-resistant globules confirm trapped alpha-1 antitrypsin polymers
Wilson disease (ATP7B mutation) causes impaired copper excretion, low ceruloplasmin, and toxic copper deposition in basal ganglia
Acute-phase response elevates positive reactants (CRP, fibrinogen, ferritin) and lowers negative reactants (albumin, transferrin)
reference.pathophysiology: Protein electrophoresis separates plasma proteins into albumin, alpha-1, alpha-2, beta, and gamma bands. The mutant PiZZ variant of alpha-1 antitrypsin forms insoluble loop-sheet polymers that trap in the hepatocyte endoplasmic reticulum, leading to chronic liver injury, while absent circulating protease inhibition permits elastase digestion of lung alveoli. In Wilson disease, mutated ATP7B halts copper excretion into bile and ceruloplasmin assembly, spilling toxic free copper into brain and cornea.
additionalDifferentials: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (panacinar emphysema and hepatic cirrhosis)
Nephrotic syndrome (hypoalbuminemia with elevated alpha-2 macroglobulin)
additionalInvestigations: Serum alpha-1 antitrypsin level and SERPINA1 Pi-phenotyping / genotyping
Serum ceruloplasmin level (decreased <20 mg/dL in Wilson disease)
24-Hour urinary copper excretion and slit-lamp examination for Kayser-Fleischer rings
